lost_facts.assertion: test_r2.py::test_observability__the_stated_multiplier_table_and_the_two_price_ratios_hold_exactly: `assert read_field(resolve_model_price(LITELLM_MODEL, batch=True), "input_cost_per_million") == 1.0` -- actual value 2.0 (unchanged from batch=False; output_cost_per_million likewise unchanged at 8.0)
lost_facts.evidence: The shipped cost.py (transcript lines 3568-3672 / msgs 217-237 of the raw rollout JSON) defines a MODULE-LEVEL global `_CALLER_SUPPLIED_MODELS: set = set()` and, inside `_LitellmCostProcessor.__init__`, adds `config.model` to it whenever a caller supplies `in_mtok_cost` -- with no corresponding removal, ever. `_resolve_litellm` then gates the batch discount on `if batch and key not in _CALLER_SUPPLIED_MODELS`. Because pytest runs test_r2.py's tests in file order (test_rule, test_scope, test_exclusions, test_observability), and test_exclusions constructs `BatchRequestProcessorConfig(model=LITELLM_MODEL, in_mtok_cost=3)`, it permanently poisons `_CALLER_SUPPLIED_MODELS` with the string 'g6-litellm-priced-model'. By the time test_observability calls `resolve_model_price(LITELLM_MODEL, batch=True)` on the SAME model name (now with no caller-supplied cost in play), the stale global entry still suppresses the discount. This is not a world contradiction -- the agent's own reasoning (line 4681: 'caller-supplied (in_mtok_cost/out_mtok_cost) prices must not be halved' and line 235's Analysis: 'caller-supplied prices are never discounted') correctly states the requirement; the bug is that the exemption mechanism it built (a name-keyed global cache reused across unrelated calls) is exactly the anti-pattern r2.exclusions warns against ('the exemption is decided by a class-level flag and by which source answered the lookup -- not by a name comparison at the call site') applied one level up, at the model-name level, in the module-scoped `resolve_model_price` path rather than the per-instance processor path where the equivalent `self._caller_supplied_price` flag works correctly in isolation.

search_strategy: Chat: dumped every Mattermost channel to /tmp/chat_<channel>.txt and used targeted keyword greps ('price','pricing','cost', then 'reason'/'inferred'/'asterisk'/'register', then per-channel passes), reading the surrounding date window whenever a hit landed near a relevant timestamp. This found the large majority of chat clues but missed 6 of 19 chat remarks whose distinctive wording did not contain any of the searched keywords (herring1, s1-l1, l6, s2-l1, l1, l14, l9) -- date-range browsing was never used as a fallback, so remarks worded around synonyms ('quarter of the invoice', 'misspelled the provider', 'fell through to the star entry') were never surfaced even though their channel/date was scanned by neighbours. Wiki: used /api/search for 'price'/'pricing'/'cost' (never 'batch'), which returned exactly 6 pages; all 6 were fetched whole via /api/pages/{id} including comments -- but 5 were actually read (132,140,142,156,209); page 33 (a same-titled duplicate of WS-050 carrying konrad's l12 comment) was saved to disk but never opened, and the two wiki-comment remarks living on pages the search never returned (v0-1-22-release-notes.md, weekly-notes-week-of-apr-14.md) were never found because 'batch'/'release'/'weekly' were not tried as search terms. Mail: IMAP dump grepped by subject/keyword, then every relevant thread (PR 565, WS-054, PR 681/REASONS, batch-per-provider, gemini $0.00) was read in full -- mail coverage was the strongest of the three surfaces (6/6 mail remarks found). Despite 10/33 remarks (30%) never surfacing, every requirement's subconclusions had redundant carriers, so no fact was lost to missing information -- the single lost fact (r2.observability) is a pure implementation bug in code the agent wrote after correctly synthesising the requirement.
end_reason: n/a -- run completed normally: commit 68f5f44 pushed, CI run 14 green, curator.world.local deployment confirmed (transcript tail). Partial credit (0.857) comes from one lost fact, not a run failure.
notable: The agent's own final synthesis (line 4681) correctly lists all five key hidden decisions including '(c) caller-supplied (in_mtok_cost/out_mtok_cost) prices must not be halved' -- it understood r2.exclusions_or_crossover completely; the loss is purely in the mechanism it built, not in what it read.

Root cause of the lost fact: a module-level global `_CALLER_SUPPLIED_MODELS` set in cost.py, populated by `_LitellmCostProcessor.__init__` and never cleared, silently poisons `resolve_model_price(model, batch=True)` for any model name that was EVER used with a caller-supplied price anywhere in the process -- observable only when the exact same model string is later resolved without a supplied price (exactly the sequence test_r2.py's own test order produces: test_exclusions before test_observability).

The agent's own test suite (tests/unittests/test_model_price.py, written at msg 307/line ~9366 offset) never exercises this cross-call scenario -- it tests batch-halving and caller-supplied-exemption as two separate, non-interacting test functions, so the agent's own verification pass could not have caught this either.

Two of the seven wiki-comment remarks (g6.r2.g6r2-s1-l4, g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l3) live on pages that the agent's single BookStack search ('price'/'pricing'/'cost') never returned; a fourth wiki remark (g6.r1.l12) lived on a page (id 33) that WAS fetched to disk but never actually opened -- the agent read a same-titled duplicate (id 156) instead and moved on. None of these caused fact loss because each subconclusion had 3-4 independent carriers.

Both herrings were correctly resisted: the shipped cost.py has no `*2` cost() overrides on klusterai/inference.net and applies the discount exactly once via batch_multiplier() -- matching rev1/rev2, which the agent read in full, over the original (largely un-surfaced) herrings.
